name: Lionheart Fixt
author: vkays
description: A cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt. Releases 0.1.0 'The Horde', 0.1.1 'The Crossroads Patrol', 0.1.2 'Standing', 0.1.4 'What Playtesting Found' 0.2.0 'What Was Written', 0.2.1, 0.3.0 'The Knights of Saladin' 0.4.0 'Quinn's Reagents', 0.5.1 'The Thieves' Guild', 0.6.0 'The Port District', 0.7.0 'The Road North', 0.8.0 'The Gate District Remainder' 0.8.1 through 0.8.4, repair releases, 0.9.0 'The Temple District', 0.9.1 'Around Barcelona', 0.9.2 through 0.9.4, repair releases, 0.10.0 'Montserrat', 0.10.1 through 0.10.3, repair releases, 0.11.0 'The Prisoner of Montserrat', 0.12.0 'La Calle Perdida', 0.13.0 'The Road North', 0.14.0 'Montaillou', 0.15.0 'Toulouse', 0.16.0 'the Crypt', and 0.17.0 'the Caverns of Nostradamus'. The goblins of the Wilderness are the most developed evil content in the game and in vanilla they feed nothing; Fixt makes the Horde a real faction with three accumulating ranks on the shipped Saladin/Templar pattern, puts back two finished characters that shipped with zero map references, and restores dialogue the original writers finished and the scripters never wired -- the Goblin Girl's cut follow behaviour, the Khan's war campaign against Barcelona, and Grumdjum's post-dryad conversation. Every check adds a route and none removes one, so the vanilla solution to every scene still works. 0.3.0 connects the Knights of Saladin's title to their rank, unlocking twenty replies across four acts, and restores the Sacred Scimitar questline -- fully authored, unstartable, and broken at all three ends. 0.4.0 is the project's first new content: three errands for Quinn the herbalist, each unlocking a healing potion tier above vanilla's Extra Healing. 0.4.1 is repair only: a structural DialogTree defect that had been silently disabling replies since 0.2.0, and two of 0.4.0's three reagent errands that could never be started. 0.5.0 'The Thieves' Guild' is the Sewers: Juanita's cut final job restored in a house built for it -- the project's first new map -- with the guard, the cell and the fee that follow being caught; the thieves' vault switched on as a real heist with five ways past its door; and Juanita's fee made unavoidable. The thieves ship four jobs to the beggars' five, pay no gold at all where Enrique pays about six hundred, and their fifth job was written, wired and left with nowhere to happen. 0.5.1 repairs two fatal crashes in 0.5.0, which was built but never published: a chest placed with an invented model path, and the same chest set to an animation its model does not have. Both killed the game on entering the vault. tools/validate.py now checks every Model= exists and every Cur Sequence= is one vanilla uses for that model; both checks were written against the real crashes. It also fixes a guard who attacked after the Speech check passed, because the reply stood down his generator rather than the man. 0.8.0 finishes the Gate District and stops there: the district's 42 orphaned replies drop to 34 and the surviving 34 are individually accounted for, none of them a cut quest. Its one real restoration is DaVinci's spirit-gem branch -- he answers being told the Inquisition has the gem, that node roots a live three-node branch holding the choice of whether to cross the Inquisition for him, and no reply led to it. Weng Choi's special-customer greeting could never fire because the conditional guarding it opens the same node on both arms, the same shape as 0.7.0's Ways Crystal. Merchant Lope's written Perception haggle was offered from nowhere and now sits beside the intimidation and Barter routes. The goblin sapper can be asked his name. Two return greetings opened their first-meeting node, the third and fourth instance of the bug 0.3.0 found on Farshad. Four further candidates were read and deliberately left alone as superseded drafts, including the Blacksmith's orphaned turn-in hub, which pays nothing a reachable node does not already pay. 0.8.1 is repair only, from the first play of three earlier features: Fernand's healing potion is now a quest item the rescue checks for by name, so it can no longer consume whatever potion the player happens to carry, and Fernand keeps acknowledging the rescue instead of forgetting it after the first time; the lava trolls are pacified at the moment they spawn rather than up to two seconds later, which closes the race that left one troll hostile at the far end of the pit; and the Helpful Wererat is named as such in conversation and turns with the rest of the beggars when they turn. 0.8.2 is repair only, from the first play of Quinn's reagent errands: a leftover test reply is removed, completed errands are no longer offered again, a turn-in with too few reagents no longer consumes them or plays the success text, the quality-pelt fix now applies from every greeting rather than one, and his reserve opens on completed errands rather than a counter that most greetings never advanced. Fernand's draught is also drinkable, so saving Juan costs a real potion. 0.8.3 repairs the Knights of Saladin: Amir now offers his Montserrat directions to a Favored One, on the greeting he actually uses after the trials, and the trials no longer strip a sworn Inquisitor or Templar of their order -- a character can hold only one faction, so Saladin content now keys on the Crescent title rather than the faction. 0.8.4 makes every skull sold to the fish monger count toward his hidden perk: bartered sales and the reduced-price sales after he declares himself full were never counted, so the fifteenth skull could not be reached. 0.9.0 is the Temple District and the first work in Act 3: an Inquisitor finally hears Torquemada's own acknowledgment for the Goblin Khan instead of the outsider's; Machiavelli keeps his promise or his threat in Montaillou, where he was on no map at all -- refuse him in Barcelona and he sells you to the Old Man's assassins at the inn, save him and he repays you; Na Roqua greets a friend of the Cathars as one, and admits she once hunted beside the shapeshifting daeva, on two voiced nodes vanilla wrote and never wired; Sir Auric sponsors a tainted initiate in the words written for one, Lord Javier tells an unsponsored petitioner to seek Auric, and Cervantes remembers you. Torquemada's own quest to purify the shadow dryad is read and left unfinished, with the reason: she cannot be killed. 0.9.1 is the areas around Barcelona: the Mongol Camp's gate guard greets a player the camp has welcomed instead of falling silent for the rest of the game, and the Irish sailor at the Port District tavern notices a down-on-their-luck drinker and hands over the clover from drowned Ireland -- a line, an icon and a Luck check the game shipped and never connected. Seven other leads around Barcelona were read and recorded as drafts. 0.9.2 is repair only, to the Port District's Fernand and Juan: Fernand now hands out his own draught (0.8.1 had repointed the Mute Sailor's reward instead), Juan spawns as a dying man rather than a corpse so the body-draining skills cannot take him and soft-lock the quest, his thanks plays before he moves, the bleed-out warns at twenty seconds, and the brothers' reunion the game wrote and never played -- Fernand's 'Claro que si!' -- plays, with three new lines of Fernand chiding him. 0.9.3 is repair only: the Vodyanoi Anatomist perk, which had never done anything, now adds 4-10 piercing to every landed hit on a vodyanoi regardless of weapon, and the Strength and Barter routes past the goblin holding the woodcutter's daughter get answers that no longer assume the player knows the Khan. 0.9.4 is a hotfix: 0.9.1's Mongol Camp gate crashed the game on entering the camp (a class name led by tabs), fixed and now caught by validate.py; and four repairs from the second playthrough -- the Knights of Saladin's cathedral summit plays and ends, Enrique's red-ore argument opens after the trade completes, the troll chief gives a hide to the player who spoke for him, and Enrique still asks for the wererat cure after his contract is withdrawn. 0.10.0 is Montserrat, the act that shipped as five maps and one conversation: human assassins and snakebreed priestesses in the packs; the Templar captain's journal at the gate, carried to whoever sent you; a wounded assassin who talks; Sahar, the rearguard's captain, with phases before Montgomerie; a mid-hall ambush, a poison tripwire, a sentry who calls for help, a trapped chest; the sanctum re-dressed as an abbey with ten hover-text stops and the monks' absence noted; and seven build levers from Sneak to the Inquisition's sealed order. Also Quinn's shop absorbing his reserve, the Desoto brothers' reunion, Juan as a dying man rather than a corpse, the Vodyanoi Anatomist perk finally working, and the Knights of Saladin's cathedral summit playing to its end. 0.10.1 is repair only: the five chests in the thieves' guild's secret stashes turned the whole guild hostile on a silent Sneak check with no line of sight and no word said; they now bark on failure and on success, both logged, and need a living thief on the map to raise the alarm, as the goblin houses' chests already did. 0.10.2 is repair only: the Inquisition jailor's Rites of Confession -- an Inquisitor's training arc with prisoners to question and a three-tier Speech lesson, built end to end and unreachable because the checker its return reply requires was never activated -- can be completed; the Templar inspection route is once-only as written; and 0.10.0's needle trap plays its sprung bark. 0.10.3 is repair only: the Templar initiation survives Esteban's death through Javier's own line, and Auric and Javier remember being attacked. 0.11.0 is The Prisoner of Montserrat: a way through the invasion that is not a fight against every pack. Give yourself up at the gate and be searched -- named weapons come back exactly, the rest as plain steel -- or keep your arms on Outwit or as one of the Master's own; wake in a new map, the abbey's undercroft, with five ways out of the cell (the lock, the pins, the handler, the drain an old monk tells you about, or wait for the escort); a garrison that stands down for a delivery and hunts a loud escape; Sahar with three ends, the third her word to carry north and a ring that Michel, Machiavelli and the Crypt's assassins each read differently; the rout on her death. Also the trolls' ore chest, the thieves' stash chests, and a Wasp Queen in the Grove's nest -- the project's first authored model. 0.10.3 is repair only: the Templar initiation survives Esteban's death through Javier's own written line, and Auric and Javier both remember being attacked -- the cathedral posting the extra guard its map built for it -- where before the maps reset and forgot. 0.12.0 is La Calle Perdida, the Wielders' hidden street: the Mad Enchanter can be told the truth and let you go; the wizards know when you have killed Relican; Cedric, Relican and Galileo remember being attacked; a Dark Wielder can break with Relican inside his own initiation and fight him -- the clone built to be unkillable is made mortal for it -- with his death closing the dark route; the four red Magic Nodes, the game's undead trials with no quest and no line, get Cedric's quest to learn what they are, a hover line each, and a ward for the report; the Inquisition's wipeout of the street kills the Wielders it generates as the shipped relay intended; Brambles thanks you three ways. Also Fernand the companion closes to arm's length before he swings, where the game had given him a spellcaster's attack range. 0.13.0 is The Road North, the maps between Montserrat and Montaillou, which were a corridor of wolves, rock titans and ogres with almost nothing to say. The spirit companions warn you about the Dark Inquisitors on the line all three of them had and none of them ever spoke; the rogues' ritual, which everyone on the map describes and nothing ever ran, finishes itself as the last of them fall, or rises bound if you join them; Shylocke's collector -- whom a player who never borrowed meets as an anonymous bandit -- says whose men they are, can be haggled, talked, guild-, Church- or perk-routed past, and no longer forgets to clear Shylocke's ledger when he is frightened off; the Inquisition's own crosses are read; a Wielder and a Dark Wielder get their own greeting at the cult's fire; a sworn Inquisitor helps Bishop Diego as a brother and can report it to Torquemada. In the mountains the ogres' charm has an end at last: both of Aka Manah's endings now lift it, and the tribe stands down across three maps. Tremblethorn's eight unreachable nodes give up the line that explains the whole area, and his second greeting stops accusing strangers of ignoring a warning he never gave. And the emptiest map on the road, the Abandoned Cave, has Bernat Sicre in it -- a Toulouse wool merchant six weeks stuck behind two hired swords, who sells what he is stuck with, tells you what Montaillou is like before you walk into it, and gets his road home when the charm breaks. 0.14.0 is Montaillou, the Cathar village with an Inquisitor sitting in it -- the densest writing left in the game, and the largest block of authored, unreachable branching the project has found: 49 reply-carrying orphan nodes, now 22, of which 16 are a deliberate duplication. The Templar knights at the gate stop you and ask your business, in the faction-aware scene the act shipped and never opened; the titans of Toulouse can be talked into letting their fugitive make his case, and he can be persuaded or tricked into going back to them, which is the ending four nodes flagged [REMOVED FROM GAME] were written for; Andre's corpse scene and his deeper first-meeting menu are reachable; Na Roqua answers a sworn Inquisitor, remembers the chicken she turned back into the mayor's wife, offers her secret stash to a friend of the Cathars and can be told what the seer said about her; the Bishop of Pamiers offers his third lead and his service to the tainted; the Cathar Warden stops accusing strangers of watching him change; Maury names the man in the square who is not to be trusted; and Lethos finally tells people to go and speak to Rhea. Then the village learns to read you: the square's mugger knows a thief of Juanita's guild, the gate knights have something to say to a man wearing the Khan's honours, the Bishop can be told by a necromancer that his tally of heretics is one short, the Cathar toughs hear an Inquisitor's confession and a Wielder's reason, the Inquisition's agent explains his plate of meat to a brother, a villager is not frightened of a tainted face, Aidan gives a trader the peace price, and the shepherd admits what he watches when he says the Bishop's name. 0.15.0 is Toulouse, the sacked town the titans are camped in, which turned out to need repair more than restoration: two checker flags the act reads and never sets, which between them cost the Speech bluff at the prisoner pen and everything the prisoners can say about the fugitive; the guard's own mercury bribe, whose success text was the act's last unreachable reply and whose designer note was its own specification; the warning the pen guard was written to give before he attacks; Menoetius, whose generator named him Rhea, so the relay that empties Toulouse and the alarm that turns the tribe on an attacker both missed him; and the news that the titans have gone, which all three endings send to Montaillou and which landed on a part that does not exist, so the village never learned. Then the act learns to read the player -- the Daeva that feeds on souls meets somebody carrying one, Rhea's history of spirit-binding meets the binding, her eater-of-memories meets a necromancer, Utnapishtim meets an Inquisitor, and Tereo, who must earn his name, meets a player who has earned one -- and the people nobody could talk to get voices: the tribe's child, the man, woman and child in the pen, and the ogres, who sell for a skin of wine what fifteen days of mutton bought nobody. 0.16.0 is act 4, the Crypt of the Bleeding Lance, whose ten maps held one quest that was only a name, four corridors with no conversation in them at all, and a two-hundred-year siege that nothing in the game let the player affect. The quest now has three states and pays out; Jehanne remembers being convinced; her doomed garrison is placed where a player actually meets it, with a camp of its own -- the project's third new map -- built around the knight who has been counting the line for two hundred and eleven years; 66 traps test a thief for the first time; the magic schools and the six claimants to the Lance each get their own answer; the four Misc Crypts become four fronts in the siege, each with a lever that moves a war tide the act's one real ending then reads three ways; Jehanne's four companion nodes, of which one was ever reachable, all work, and the garrison can finally tell whether she is walking beside the player who is cutting them down; and the Spirit Council, which always described the player's borrowed soul in a single voice, now says which of the three it sees, and can tell whom it is begging. 0.17.0 is act 5, the Caverns of Nostradamus, where the shipped game had two quests and no way into either: both hang on one conversation with a Hujark general whose generator was switched off and activated by nothing, so every player who has ever walked the act fought the Hujark on a map set built to be populated either way. He spawns now, and so does the English army that was designed, statted, tiered, given archers and placed nowhere -- fourteen units in a folder called 'English in Caverns of Nostrodomus', now fielded by ninety-nine generators across nine maps, switched on by the call vanilla was already making. Side with the Hujark and they stand aside while the English hunt you; side with the English and the act is the one that shipped; or talk your way past at Speech 75 and cross somebody else's war with a safe conduct only half the combatants recognise, which is revocable the moment you raise a hand to a Hujark. The seer defends himself with the four spells and three taunts he was built with and nothing ever started; a shield-helmet swordsman at half health calls a snake out of the floor, unless you carry Sahar's ring, because the serpents know her mark; a snakebreed summoner at a quarter health calls something much worse, which the ring does not stop; forty-three traps appear in ten maps of caves that never held one; the frightened apprentice stops turning up alive on the next map after you kill him; and the act reads your race, your spirit, your school, your reputation and, if you have the title, refuses to shake your hand at all. 0.18.0 is act 6, the Barcelona Attack, the shortest act in the game and the one with the least left in it: eight maps, 889 live combatants and twenty-eight player replies in total, of which two were gated on anything, so the work is less about unreachable branching than about a city that never reacted to the person walking through it. Crossroads Siege -- 910 parts and 472 live combatants, four times the Crypt's Doomed Plateau and the densest map in the project -- shipped with no conversation, no balloon and no dialogue tree at all, and now says what the field, the standard and the road west are, and carries the relay that makes English soldiers shout, which existed on both district maps and not on the one map the English army is actually on. Two of the act's three quests were never written: Find Galileo and DaVinci shipped with a blank Name= and no states, the True Cross pursuit has a name and no states, and neither was referenced by any map or tree in the game; the blacksmith answers where the two inventors went, and because he says they were marched out the west gate with a guard who had a list, the fresh ruts at the crossroads become a ground lens and a wax tablet rather than scenery. The Child Killer title -- display name Slayer of Innocents, described, read eight times on the peacetime Gate District, driving five fully authored dialogue nodes with two replies each -- is granted for the first time in the game's history, from 34 citizen generators on the idiom Merchant Slayer already uses 28 times; children are not made killable, because they are HP 10000 / AC 1000 by deliberate design and the perk's own words are killing the helpless. Act 6 then reads it on the two checker parts it was already carrying and never touched, so the man searching the district for his son stops accusing every stranger who speaks to him of having done enough -- and there is a boy in a red cap behind a barrel to find, told to stay where he was put. Shy Girl requests help, a relay sitting active with zero callers, positioning a balloon over an entity that did not exist and firing a relay that did not exist either, is whole again, and ends in the shipped Spaniards Attack Player so that murdering a civilian in front of a witness costs what attacking a guard costs. Two dying-soldier lines nothing opened are wired, the Spaniard hands over the 250 gold he is talking about, and Temple District Siege's 62 mute corpses give up six voices. Then the act learns to read the player, where before it read PE 8, Speech 70 and a Sneak check: Surrey O'Connell, the Irish supplies master pressed into feeding the army that took his country, stops performing for anyone carrying the clover from the drowned fields of Ireland and for a sworn Inquisitor, and either way looks the other way at the Regent's chest -- two new routes past the act's one guarded prize; the blacksmith reads your order, your face and your reputation; and the Church Crypt, thirteen parts of wall, lamp, broken door and one dead guard, gets the act's first secret, first trap, first hidden lock and first voice. 0.18.1 puts Slayer of Innocents on the hooks the designers built for it. 0.18.0 awarded the title for murdering an unarmed citizen, because children cannot be killed -- Races/NPCs/Generic Child is AC 1000 / HP 10000 and every child in the game uses that one race -- and that reading missed the mechanism the designers did build: each child's generator carries a working CSetDamagedScriptActionAction, so hitting one has always been detected even though killing one is not. Five children across six placements, every hook already doing real work -- the woodcutter's daughter screams, flees, turns the goblin on you, deletes the whole peaceful-resolution script set, fails the woodcutter's quest, activates a flag her father's dialogue reads, and reaches across maps to delete her generator at the house; Marisol's hook fails Find the lost boy Tomas in the Sewers; the shepherd's son activates Player hurt the son and Make Maury mad for hurting son -- and not one of them touched the title the game wrote for exactly this. The grant now sits in all six with every vanilla action left in place, and everything downstream already worked: it reaches the guards' 2 Childkiller Intro, whose 'I am the killer' reply fires both Damage a guard in the city district and Child killer bubble text, the guard shouting 'Have at thee, monster!' The hooks cannot misfire, because nothing on those four maps can target a neutral, so the goblin over the daughter and the trolls over Tomas cannot earn the player a title. The citizen grant stays alongside: 40 grants in total, 34 citizen generators and 6 child hooks. 0.19.0 is act 7, the English Shrine, which the project's tester calls the worst section in the game -- all combat with the same three or four enemies and nothing to do but wander and fight -- and the numbers agree: Soldier alone is 1,496 of the act's 2,048 spawn entries, 73% of everything, and the act fields 19 enemy families where the Crypt has 82, with two conversations across eleven maps, one quest with one state and one unique item between the fights. The act's own enemies were in the files and used nowhere: the shrine's enemy faction is the Druids, the one line a rank-and-file enemy speaks is about awakening the dragon, and the Druid template is fielded nowhere, so every druid in the act was a generic English soldier; three Priestess templates are placed nowhere in the entire game while Druid Master, the act's boss, has the race Priestess Super, so the order she leads never appeared in its own shrine. All of them are fielded now through 195 weighted entries on existing generators across nine maps, deepest-first, with no spawner count changed and no vanilla spawn dropped. The Priestess ladder shipped unfinished -- AC 260/80/150 against the Priest line's 230/250/280, and no damage resistance at any tier -- so its spell identity is kept and only the defences repaired, and the Druid Master, who shipped on the rank-and-file race at HP 95 / AC 150 against an Assassin Master on her own map at HP 400, gets a boss's race. Act 7 had no merchant on any of its eleven maps, so there are two Templar posts now on the act's own unplaced Knight Templar template -- a quartermaster whose stock is gated on the same three quest checks Quinn the herbalist uses for his own reserve, so errands run in act 1 are still paying out six acts later; a field surgeon who treats a Templar or a Knight of Saladin free and charges everyone else including a sworn Inquisitor; and a guard who finally speaks the one dialogue tree in the act that nothing opened. The whole post is gated on having accepted Sir Roger's help, so refusing him costs something for the first time. Helping Guy Fawkes in act 1 is recorded at last as the title Servant of the Queen, where before the allegiance was stored nowhere and the only later act to touch the quest was act 6, which failed it in a bulk list; Sir Roger reads it and tells such a player that the Queen keeps druids and his Order came to the shrine without her leave, and Surrey O'Connell gets a third and colder route past the Regent's chest beside 0.18.0's clover and Holy Office. And on the landing beach, Captain Isabella's inactive generator turns out to guard a complete, voice-recorded arrival-in-England arc with eleven orphaned nodes -- she is Grace O'Malley, an Irish pirate two years in disguise, and she can be found, recruited, romanced and left behind, with two of her recordings renamed out of reach until now, so all 38 are audible and both companions' trees have zero orphan nodes; act 1 gains the beat her romance was missing, and answering it is what the romance requires. Eight combat barks that never played do, and the Inner Sanctum -- 88 enemies and not one word on the map -- turns out to be a three-switch vault whose doors sit up to 800 units from their switches, so it now says what it is and each stone reports what it opened. 0.20.0 is act 8, Alamut, the last act and by a distance the biggest -- eleven maps and 15,498 level parts, more than acts 6 and 7 together -- and the opposite of act 7 in every way that matters: 88 enemy families across 131 templates with a top-four share of 53%, the most varied act in the back half of the game, 63 real traps and 46 hidden areas. What it lacked was words and wiring. 05 Acid Wash shipped with no dialogue tree and no balloon at all, 334 parts and not one line, while carrying a cycling hazard whose mechanism is a sluice: crossing a trigger clones a walking acid front that cuts the ground away as it travels and spawns 20-to-40 Acid steam around itself, the floor is restored six seconds later, and the gate re-arms ten seconds after that, against ranged-only opposition of fifteen archers and twelve master spellcasters who never come down into the channel. It says what it is now, warns before each wash, states the ten seconds, and reports what the disarm switch shut off. The goblin companion 0.2.0 deferred to this act by name is in: all twelve of Grumdjum's 300-series nodes are voice-recorded, every one of them, and CSetCompanionAction in his tree counted zero while the node the whole cluster hangs off was opened by nothing -- so he joins, quips in rhyming couplets, calls for healing at half and a fifth of his health, can be dismissed and taken back, and the Khan himself turns up in the dunes as a cameo whose three recorded lines shipped with the voiceover flag switched off. Both goblins answer to goblin rank: be the Horde's Champion and leave their Khan breathing, or kill him for Torquemada in act 1 and no goblin comes to Alamut at all, six acts later. The Knight of Saladin's arc half worked -- recruiting him the first time you met him set the companion flag without the escort AI, so he stood where he was and then asked whether he should rejoin, and nothing in his tree could dismiss him at all -- and his companion race carried melee 200 against HP 150 and AC 145, the weakest companion in the game placed in the final act, so the defence is repaired to 220 and 215 and the offence left alone. And the last act now knows who arrived at it: every gate in it was a skill or karma threshold, one title perk of seventeen was read anywhere in the act, and the four orders were read only to pick a greeting, so the Old Man gets a line of defiance per order drawn from that order's own history with the Assassins -- Saladin's tent and the two knives that found nothing, the Temple's sixty years of tribute, the Inquisitor who has burned men for a tenth of that heresy, and the Goblin Champion counting himself the Khan's second attempt -- and the Knight of Saladin finally answers the order he already greets. Three reads closed without a build and are recorded so they are not re-opened: the ending matrix is alive and all fourteen of its relays fire, the Old Man's orphaned escape line is a superseded draft of the one that plays, and both dragons are placed and fought. 0.21.0 begins from a review that asked whether the additions to the Crypt and to England had actually broken up the combat they were meant to break up, and the answer measured by placement rather than volume was no: the Crypt received eighteen parts across eleven maps of which twenty-two of twenty-six dialogue placements are balloons with no replies, one conversation, no merchant, no healer and no change to what spawns, and its one real respite is a dead-end side room off the first map, reached before any of the act and followed by two thousand seven hundred spawn entries of narration. So this release does the other thing instead, on the tester's idea: the Doomed Plateau's undead get captains. The largest piece of finished-but-unfielded creature content the project has found turns out to be the Boss Lich -- three races, a sprite and seventeen animations, better animated than monsters the game ships, with no character template anywhere pointing at any of it, so nothing could ever spawn it. Its races are a designed encounter rather than a stat bump: an enormous pool at armour class eighty, so trivial to hit and very slow to fall, immune to cold and poison and disease, hardening against electrical and piercing as it tiers, and fire left deliberately weakest at every tier. It is fielded now as the Bonecaller, and it is the one captain that can be reasoned with, because a lich commands and remembers: Wielder standing, Divine magic or Speech opens it, and it is bound to a siege whose author is long dead -- the pointing has outlived the hand, and it cannot put the order down. Release it and the horde turns on it and it fights back; or, with karma low enough, swear to it instead and it walks at the keep with you while the Templar garrison turns on it, which closes the garrison's own offer to take you in and leaves nothing to say to the knights but a threat. Anyone may free it. Only the wicked may recruit it. Beside it stand two captains that cannot be talked to and are interesting in other ways: the Bonewright, whose own designed race had been abandoned so that it shipped at half strength on a generic ghoul stat block, and which raises the fallen for as long as it stands so that the endless stream finally has a source and a lever; and the Revenant Sergeant, who opens the fight ignoring you because you are not yet the problem, whistles its section off the knights and onto you at two thirds, and at a third abandons the battle altogether to come for you alone through its own dead. 0.21.1 comes out of asking whether 0.15.0 did enough in the Pyrenees, and finding that the Shapeshifting Daeva -- a nemesis that tracks the player across Barcelona, Toulouse and Montaillou, reacts to which relic of Zarathustra they carry, and can be talked down at Speech 95, which makes it one of only four talk-instead-of-fight encounters in the game -- had never been touched at all, with 27 orphan nodes across its two trees. Its Ring variant was written and never heard: the confrontation is gated on carrying the Ring or the Amulet and then always played the Amulet's line, so the Ring's own reaction sat unused, and with it the entire Speech route for anyone who brought the Ring instead. Its escape from Montaillou was silent, because the relay that does the mechanical work never spoke the line written for it, while Toulouse's matching line plays. And the fight cannot be won without a relic at all: killing the third or fourth disguised form re-arms six clone generators with no condition attached, while the true form -- the only version that stays dead -- is raised by nothing but the relic check, which is why it taunts that you lack the power to truly defeat it. So the Daeva of Pain, imprisoned under a Barcelona church, finally pays a debt the game already promised out loud when it said its judgment would be swift and merciless but that to you it owed something. What he owes depends on which service was done: lure the wizard to him and he arrives in Montaillou, trades barbs with her across a camera before they fight, and brings her true form up stripped of the twenty-odd hit points a second it heals; break the crosses yourself and he waits instead at the spot where a spirit companion says something is ahead, and gives up her name, which opens the talk route to a character who never found a relic. Refuse him and it closes again. Kill him back in Barcelona and none of it happens. 0.22.0 is what came of asking what act 7 offers a character who did not build for combat. Nothing, as it turned out, and not for the reason expected: the act is not combat-gated anywhere, since every transition poly on the critical path is open at map load, the four shut ones are optional side rooms opened by using a door, Stop the Druids completes on the Alamut crossing poly, and nothing in the game records or checks whether the Druid Master died -- so a character who never swings a weapon can already walk past the boss and be told they stopped the druids. What was missing was any reason to have built a talker or a thief, because inside the shrine there is not one Speech, Barter, Lockpick or Sneak check in 208 replies. The Druid Master, the only act boss in the game with no alternative to the fight, can now be talked off the ley lines at Speech 130 using her own lore against her -- Richard closed the Disjunction with his blood and is buried one chamber away, and she means to open the lines nine paces from his grave with the only living Lionheart in the room. She also finally reads who is refusing her: her offer to destroy the Inquisition had been pitched in identical words to a sworn Inquisitor, to a Wielder who wants precisely that, and to a Templar and a Knight of Saladin. Sneak does something for the first time since the Sewers: of the game's four Sneak requirement cans only one was ever referenced, twice, both in act 1, and the other three now open the temple's secret passage, which skips two maps and a thousand spawns, and spot the ambush waiting behind the wall of the last chamber. That ambush check reads the live sneak toggle as well as the skill, the way Toulouse does -- Titan Village holds the only three checks in the shipped game against it, and they drive the best stealth encounter in the game. Finally a repair that is this project's own fault: the map builder omitted the field that lets a trigger re-arm after the player walks out of it, which vanilla writes on 756 touching triggers out of 756, and twelve Fixt triggers had shipped unable to fire on a second visit -- ten of them the charm sweeps that are supposed to lift once you have broken the ogre charm elsewhere. 0.23.0 answers a question about act 8: the desert is the Knights of Saladin's own country, and choosing that order bought less there than choosing any other. Its identity checks ran Templar 13, Inquisitor 12, Goblin Champion 4, Saladin 6 -- and three of those six were one greeting selector. The Knight of Saladin who meets you at the dunes is handed to everybody, and membership bought a salutation. Underneath that sat a ladder nothing read: every order has three rungs, each granting permanent modifiers and a point of rank, and Saladin's top rung is Exalted, the strongest faction perk in the game, reached only by taking the Dream Djinni initiation, Jafar's errand and all five green Way Crystals. The canned requirement that tests for it is referenced by nothing in the shipped game, and neither are the Templar or Inquisitor equivalents; the only faction ladder anything reads is the Goblin Horde's, which this project built in 0.1.0. So act 8 now reads it. The knight greets an Exalted as a superior and tells one what the order does not say in its chapter houses: the oath every Aswaran takes and never hears again, that if the Old Man moves on the Sultan's house a third time the highest of them who is nearest rides and does not come back with prisoners, and that in eighty years nobody has ever been nearest. The Old Man answers the rank beside the line he already had for a Goblin Champion. And the order rides: the knight existed on exactly one map and stopped at the fortress door, and now comes through the Maw, the Acid Wash, the Chamber of Torment and the Dark Temple, stopping at the Old Man's chamber because of the oath he quoted. Two more things in the same desert. The merchant, the most expensive in the game at a multiplier of 2, recognises the order and takes half a point off it, stacking with his haggling, and he finally stocks the three healing tiers 0.4.0 unlocked, which until now existed only in Barcelona. And Fazeem's bird men, whose encounter is a confidence trick requiring a merchant's tip, Speech 70, Barter and Intelligence to convince them that Assassin blood makes rain, can simply be told the truth by a knight whose order is in that desert to kill Assassins -- the same bargain, without the lie, and without the money the lie earns. 0.24.0 comes out of an objection to 0.23.0: nothing in this game should be only a benefit, and by then the Knights of Saladin were the purest upside in it. An audit of all five allegiances found that the Inquisition pays for itself everywhere -- 25 percent more at the Barcelona herbalist, 50 at the Montaillou weird woman, 10 at the rogue in the Plains, and the Cathars and the shepherd and the witch all withhold from it -- while the Wielders answer to the Montaillou mayor and to Beatrice and to the Crypt captains. Against that, the Temple had exactly one cost in the whole game, the Goblin Horde had one bark, and the Order of Saladin had nothing at all: every one of its 42 checks is a welcome, a thanks or a piece of information. The three of them now cost something, each in the place the game had already written the grievance and never connected. The Bishop of Pamiers lets a Knight of Saladin introduce himself, which no vanilla reply allowed, and the introduction is the price -- he writes the Order into the register he is in Montaillou to keep, and the gate guard who used to call you an ally of the Temple stops being glad to see you, without closing the gate, because the alliance is real and the game says so. The Cathar toughs in the tavern pick their fight over one grievance, that the priests and their friends eat the village food, and three rooms away the Templar knights are demanding more ale from the mayor by right of the code; a Knight Templar may no longer claim he is not one of them, and settling it costs 150 gold or a brawl. And Alvaro at the Crossroads, who already sorts beggars by race, now knows what the Horde did to his carts and charges it back at 1.5 -- so a sworn goblin buys at 0.75 from the warren vendor and 1.5 from the people whose road he raided. 0.25.0 'What They Were Built To Do' is the first release aimed at how enemies fight rather than at what they say, and every piece of it is a creature using an ability it already had. `CNormalAttackAI.Minimum Attack Distance` is the whole archetype system -- 391 of 478 monster cans walk up and swing -- and `Shoot Completed`, the slot deciding what a creature does on each attack, is empty or skill-less in 400 of them. The Priestess is the Priest with one field missing: a line-by-line diff of the two cans differs in exactly one place, and her race already presets up to four offensive spells at 95 that she had never cast in twenty-three years. All three tiers now cycle through exactly what their own race knows, using the shuffled-series idiom 67 shipped files already use rather than a re-roll that can hand out the same spell four times running. The Boss Lich, fielded as the Bonecaller in 0.21.0, raises the dead one attack in four by the same clone-and-checker idiom two shipped ghouls use, on a map that already carried both parts. And the thieves of Barcelona backstab: the gate was traced in the executable and is four conditions on whoever is attacking, with no player or party test anywhere, so the perk was player-only by data rather than by code. Vanilla ships eighteen thief races that nothing references, a name-for-name match with the eighteen thief cans and evasive where the thug races they actually wear are sturdy; twenty-four melee thief cans are repointed onto twelve of them, and those carry the two attributes the gate reads. Archers are left out, because the gate needs a melee attack type. The Old Man of the Mountain was read and deliberately left alone: he turns into the dragon, and his forty hit points are a stage direction. 0.25.1 is repair only, and urgent: releases 0.19.0 through 0.25.0 could not reach the main menu. Grace O'Malley's race, authored in 0.19.0, preset a skill called `Skills/Fighting/Melee`, which has never existed -- the real one is `OneHandedMelee` -- and the engine resolves race skill presets at load, so it was fatal on every launch rather than on the right save. The gate that should have caught it had two gaps that lined up: it scanned only dialogue trees, maps and cans, so race files were never examined, and it had no reference kind for `Skill=`, `Race=` or `Derived Character Attribute=` even if they had been. Both are closed, and a sweep of 376 references of those kinds across every Fixt file found exactly the one defect. 0.25.2 is repair only, and fatal: a `.DialogTree` may not name its own file, and eleven sites across four characters did. The loader recurses and the game dies, so Captain Isabella, Grace, Brambles, Grumdjum and the Alamut knight could not be spoken to at all. Vanilla never does this -- all four of its in-tree tree references name a different file -- so every offender was this project's, shipped in 0.12.0, 0.19.0 and 0.20.0 and never loaded by anyone because the game could not start from 0.19.0 onward. Each offending action is moved verbatim into a `CCannedObject` and fired with `CUseCannedActionAction`, which is the indirection the engine's own error message asks for and which the shipped game uses 107 times; nothing around it changes, and no map is edited. Gate 0 now rejects any tree that names itself.
